desc:
Each rectangle [x1, y1, x2, y2] is axis-aligned, with its bottom-left corner at (x1, y1) and its top-right corner at (x2, y2), where x1 < x2 and y1 < y2. Rectangles may overlap, nest or touch.

Return the total area of the plane covered by at least one rectangle (each point counted once), modulo 1,000,000,007.

rects = [[0, 0, 2, 2], [1, 1, 3, 3]]  ->  7
rects = [[0, 1, 3, 2], [1, 0, 2, 3]]  ->  5

The first example is two 2x2 squares sharing a 1x1 corner: 4 + 4 - 1 = 7. The second is a plus shape made of a 3x1 and a 1x3 rectangle.
constraints: rects[i] = [x1, y1, x2, y2] with 0 ≤ x1 < x2 ≤ 10<sup>9</sup> and 0 ≤ y1 < y2 ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>
The true area can reach 10<sup>18</sup>, hence the modulo
hints: Inclusion-exclusion over rectangles explodes. Instead, slice the plane into vertical strips between consecutive x-coordinates of rectangle edges.
In a strip, every rectangle either spans the whole strip or does not touch it. So the area of the strip is its width times the total length of the union of the y-ranges of the active rectangles.

Sweep over x. At x1 add the y-range, at x2 remove it. Maintain the covered y-length with a segment tree over the compressed y-coordinates: each node stores a cover count and the covered length of its range, and counts are never pushed down.
editorial: Sweep a vertical line from left to right. Between two consecutive event x-coordinates, the set of active rectangles is fixed, so the covered area of that strip equals (xnext - x) × coveredLength, where coveredLength is the length of the union of the active y-intervals.

Compress all y-coordinates; the elementary pieces between neighbouring y-values are the leaves of a segment tree. Each node keeps cnt, the number of active rectangles that cover the node's whole range (and are registered exactly at that node), and cov, the covered length inside the node: if cnt > 0 it is the full length of the node's range, otherwise the sum of the children's cov (0 for a leaf). Adding a rectangle increments cnt on O(log n) canonical nodes and removing it decrements the same nodes, so no lazy propagation is needed.

Process the 2n events sorted by x, add cov[root] × (x - previousX) to the area before each event batch, then update the tree. O(n log n) time and O(n) space. Take the result modulo 109+7 at the end (exact Python integers cannot overflow).
